root_motivation: **Who:** a coding agent in a terminal (Claude Code, Codex), a CI job calling host.spec.test, Joe probing prod. **What:** one command per host tool with typed flags and machine output, no JSON by hand. **Why not today:** the mcphost binary has server-side subcommands only; every shell interaction with the host is a hand-typed tool name and argument object. The command table is generated from the embedded contract, so the shell cannot name a tool or argument the host does not serve.
user_persona: A coding agent in a shell that publishes, tests and calls host tools with typed flags and exit codes; a CI job gating on exit status; Operator Joe warned of contract skew against prod.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given the embedded contract, When the clap tree is built, Then Command::debug_assert passes and fewer than 5 canonical tools needed any override; the test prints the override list and fails the premise at 5.
Given `mcphost call host.tool.publish --name x --kind nope --spec-json '{}'`, When parsed, Then clap exits 2 before any network with the schema's kind enum in the message.

Given a running test host and MCPHOST_KEY set, When `mcphost call host.tool.publish --name hello --kind python --spec-json @fixture.json --json` runs, Then stdout is one JSON line equal to the host's structuredContent and the key never appears in argv, stdout or stderr.

Given a host returning args_invalid, bearer_invalid, tool_exception and a 503, When each is received, Then the exit codes are 2, 4, 3, 5 and stderr carries error_code and data; the mapping test covers every AppError::code() arm.

Given a test host whose /contract.json ETag differs from the embedded sha, When any call runs, Then stderr's first line is `contract skew: binary 1.<12> host 1.<12>` and the call still proceeds; with --no-skew-check no HEAD is sent.

Given the contract and the CLI tree, When the drift test compares subcommand names, flag names and help text, Then all three sets are equal; one tool removed from the embedded contract fails the test naming it.
Given `mcphost call --completions zsh`, When sourced in zsh, Then `mcphost call host.r<TAB>` lists host.redeem, host.registry.publish, host.runs.*.

Given prod, When the CLI calls an anonymous tool with no key, Then it prints the plan ceilings and exits 0 (Live; evidence: `mcphost call host.quickstart --url https://mcphost.dev --json | jq -e '.limits.plan.budget != null'`)
acceptance_criteria.test: deferred -- operator-provisioned: live `mcphost call host.quickstart --url https://mcphost.dev --json` against prod after deploy.

scope: src/call_cli.rs (new): the contract-built clap tree, alias rewrite, argument JSON, run, --list and --completions rendering.
src/client.rs (new): the streamable-HTTP client extracted from compat_check.rs, plus the error-code -> exit-code table.
src/main.rs: `mcphost call` dispatched before the derive parser; Command::Call for --help.
Cargo.toml: clap gains the string and env features.
non_goals: Tenant-published tools as subcommands; interactive prompts; storing keys; replacing the dev-loop verbs; nested typed flags for object arguments.

additional.key_never_a_flag: tenant_key is the Authorization bearer from MCPHOST_KEY or --key-file, never a flag value.

five_whys_trace.q: Why can a shell not call a host tool today?
five_whys_trace.a: The binary has only server-side subcommands, so an agent hand-types JSON-RPC.

five_whys_trace.q: Why not a hand-written client table?
five_whys_trace.a: A second copy of the contract drifts; the table is generated from the embedded contract and a drift test pins it.

ambiguities_resolved.question: 188 canonical tools?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: The embedded contract has 170 canonical dotted tools; the underscore wire names and registered aliases are accepted on input and rewritten.

ambiguities_resolved.question: AC3 kind python?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: The real-host test publishes kind echo (python needs the userns sandbox); the stub-host test pins the python request shape.
